title: Turning long videos into retrievable episodic memory
description: Published approaches for structuring and retrieving events from long-form video.

report.question: can I turn long videos into episodic memories and how easy will it be to retrieve this memories when needed?
report.reasoning: Long videos can be successfully structured into episodic and semantic memories using frameworks such as TELEMEM and WorldMM. Systems like TELEMEM organize long-term memory into directed acyclic graphs and achieve high retrieval accuracy, scoring 86.33% on the ZH-4O benchmark.
openQuestions: How well do these memory architectures generalize to extremely long videos beyond standard benchmarks without degrading retrieval precision?
What are the exact computational costs associated with continuous online video segmentation and knowledge graph consolidation?

agents.name: Researcher A
agents.summary: Systems like TELEMEM and WorldMM allow long videos to be structured into episodic and semantic memories for reasoning and retrieval. TELEMEM achieves a 43% token reduction compared to Mem0 and outperforms standard RAG and other memory baselines on long-horizon reasoning tasks.

agents.name: Researcher B
agents.summary: Long videos can be turned into episodic and semantic memories using frameworks like WorldMM, M3-Agent, and TELEMEM, which extract structured representations such as RDF triples or DAG nodes. Retrieving these memories typically relies on multi-turn agentic loops or closure-based traversal. However, retrieval effectiveness varies significantly depending on the complexity of the query and the memory architecture used.

agents.name: Contradiction Hunter
agents.summary: Systems such as WorldMM and TELEMEM demonstrate that long videos can indeed be structured into episodic and semantic memories, which can then be retrieved using multi-turn or graph-traversal RAG strategies. However, retrieval ease and accuracy vary significantly depending on the underlying architecture and the complexity of the video domain.

agents.name: Evidence Auditor
agents.summary: Evidence indicates that long videos can be structured into episodic and semantic memories using systems like WorldMM and TELEMEM, and retrieved using multi-turn agentic loops or DAG closure. However, current retrieval and memory systems do not guarantee high accuracy on long-horizon reasoning benchmarks, where even the best evaluated models achieve relatively low scores. The provided evidence does not show a direct head-to-head comparison between all memory frameworks under identical benchmark settings.
